paper_title: Known By Their Actions: Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces
fingerprinting_target: LLMs are being identified by their actions alone from performing tasks on Wikipedia and Amazon
trajectory_type: Clicks, scrolls, keypresses, timings, and focus navigations are recorded
input_signal_features: Events for every click, scroll, keydown, and navigation; wait time in-between events; scroll depths; click positions; events per page; search-box frequencies
method: XGBoost on 14 agents; behavior features only; no access to question text or page content
main_finding: A classifier that has been trained on 14 different LLMs is able to identify an agent from few actions on a webpage with up to 96\% F1 accuracy.
limitations: Classifier performs worse when transferring single tasks across websites, as opposed to in-domain attribution. Classifier also performs worse with randomized time delays between agent actions. Only two websites are used (amazon & wikipedia) and they are not honeypot websites.
replication_suitability: ✅: All steps and data provided in detail on GitHub.
